title: Pip Finds a Fluffy Cloud
markdown:
Skye lived in a tiny snug house. Its roof felt like a soft green pillow. Her home sat in the Starberry Hills, which sparkled like diamonds. The air smelled like sweet berries and warm sunshine. Skye’s best friend was a little mouse named Pip. Pip was white and soft, like a snowflake. Whiskers wiggled. Eyes sparkled like morning dew. They loved their cosy home. Today, Skye had a new idea.

“Pip, my little Pip!” Her voice a tinkling bell. “Today, I will teach you a special trick! It will be very helpful!” She imagined Pip bringing acorn hats when they fell from the trees. Then her tummy did a little flip-flop. What if Pip didn’t like it? What if she couldn’t teach him at all? Chin tucked, lip nibbled. Pip was so very small. What if it was too tricky?

But today was the Starberry Festival. If Pip didn’t learn to fetch hats, Skye would have to run all the way back and forth herself when they tumbled down. So, Pip safe in her hands, they went to the edge of the mossy bell-fern wood. Ferns curled like green question marks. They tiptoed past. Tall trees made gentle shadows. “This will be a quiet spot for practice!” A happy sigh.

She set Pip down beside a smooth grey stone, cool. “Now, Pip, watch me!” A red acorn hat, rolled from an oak. “Fetch, Pip! Fetch the hat!” Pip wiggled his nose. Whiskers twitched. He looked at the hat. Then he saw soft green moss, a velvet blanket. He padded over. Nudged the moss. Squeak? he seemed to ask. Skye let out a soft sigh. “Oh, Pip, no, not the moss. The hat! The lovely red hat.”

Then a tiny beetle, shell like a little jewel, hurrying along a twig. Pip watched. A little wobble in Skye’s tummy. She wished they had stayed home, where everything was warm and familiar.

A kind voice, rustling leaves. “Hullo there, little ones!” A wizard into the clearing, like a kind grandfather, beard long and swirly, backpack that might pop, full of colours. “My, what a wonderful mouse you have!” Eyes twinkling. “I’m Mr. Glimmerchalk. I collect pretty colours!” He opened the pack a tiny bit. Chalk sticks of yellow, blue, and green.

Skye’s tummy felt a little better. “I’m trying to teach Pip to fetch my acorn hats, Mr. Glimmerchalk, but he gets distracted.” A chuckle like soft pebbles rolling. “Ah, yes. It’s common! What we think is useful isn’t always what our friends are best at finding.” He looked closely at Pip, who was watching a tall dandelion. “Your mouse likes soft fluffy things. See how he’s looking at that dandelion puff?”

A fluffy white puff, ready to fly. Pip’s eyes wide with wonder. “Go on, Pip,” Skye whispered. “See what you can do with that fluffy thing.” He scampered. He didn’t grab. He nudged gently. Batted with his paws. Squeak! Happily. The puff floated down like a tiny feather. Pip chased it. Pushed it to Skye’s feet.

Not an acorn hat, not at all. But he had brought it with so much joy. Her plan for a useful trick was very different from this wonderful surprise. And Pip was so happy.

“Oh, Pip!” She scooped him up. Hats forgotten. “You found a tiny cloud for me! A real fluffy cloud!” Pip snuggled. The puff rested beside them. Mr. Glimmerchalk smiled. “He’s very good at finding softness. Sometimes wonderful discoveries are the ones we never planned.” A wave. “Enjoy your fluffy cloud. It’s a treasure.” Another chuckle, and he walked away.

Home. Pip trotted beside Skye, nudging the puff, which bobbed and weaved like a dancer. The woods didn’t seem shadowy now. Friendly. Full of surprises.

Safe and warm, Skye didn’t worry about acorn hats. She stroked Pip’s fur. He was perfect just as he was. He didn’t need to fetch hats. He was a master at finding fluffy delights. Pip curled on her lap, sighed. The dandelion puff sat on the table like a guest. Tomorrow there would still be hats on the ground. Tonight there was a cloud, which was enough.
